# `spec.set`: Set spec

Creates or replaces a Model Spec (named parts, shapes, anchors, joins) and compiles it into one object per part.

- Category: spec
- Version: 1
- Complexity: the changed parts' build costs, plus O(mesh size) per part for fingerprints
- Flags: undoable, creates_groups, creates_objects
- Also known as: model spec, spec, blueprint, declarative model, parts

The spec is the model's source; meshes are build artifacts. Each part has one shape (`sdf`, `primitive`, `lathe`, `sweep`, `loft`, `extrude`, `pipe`, `mirror` or `instance`), a placement (`transform`, or an `anchor` on another part's surface: a landmark such as `top` or `ear_root_l`, a `param`, a `ray` or `nearest`), a `join` (`separate`, `blend` for SDF parts, `decal`) and optional `edits` (ops run on the part). Parts compile in dependency order; unchanged parts are reused, so later patches are fast. Every face records the spec node that made it. An `archetypes` block (`{"dwarf": {"kind": "dwarf"}}`) expands into a skeleton whose joints are landmarks and into generated parts you patch by name.

**Use for** building a model from parts and relations instead of op sequences; patch it with `spec.patch`.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | required | Name of the spec's root object; it holds one object per part. An existing spec root of that name gets the new spec. |
| `parent` | `string \| null` | - | Parent object of a new root; top level when omitted. |
| `position` | `[Length, Length, Length] \| null` | - | Position of a new root in its parent's space. |
| `spec` | `unknown` | required | The Model Spec: `{"parts": {"head": {"sdf": [...]}, "ear_l": {...}}}` (see the spec guide). |

## Examples

```json
{"name":"lamp","spec":{"parts":{"base":{"primitive":{"cylinder":{"height":0.02,"radius":0.1}}},"pole":{"anchor":{"landmark":"top","on":"base"},"primitive":{"cylinder":{"height":0.4,"radius":0.01}}}}}}
```

Result: `spec lamp (o:1): 2 parts, 2 built, 0 unchanged
  base (cylinder) 200 x 20 x 200 mm at (0, 10, 0) mm, 112 faces
  pole (cylinder) 20 x 400 x 20 mm at (0, 220, 0) mm, 32 faces`
